title: The Right Hand and the Left Hand
english: God transfers men from the earthly place to the high heavens. If he says 'work', he does not mean it by number, but by kind or even by genus. In their light—for we take the fathers to be wise—we say that in the days which they had, being dazzled by the true light of the sun of righteousness, it became a work in the light of their life, which they were not envious to share with us.

He said, and he remembers: seven nations under the later called holy land he brought down (Ps 105:23). They were hidden, having been led in by God into that land. Moses, therefore, without neglect, prays to repeat the mystery: 'Having led them in, hide them in the mountain of your inheritance, O holiness, Lord, which your hands prepared' (Ex 19:4). See that no one living externally and hearing is able to enter into the holy mountain. The crowds in the parables, therefore, hearing and being outside, did not enter into the holy mountain, where the parables were made clear. It is necessary, therefore, to be led in first, and then thus to be hidden.

Your hand destroyed nations, and you hid them. Not of God in the ancient days. He was ancient of days (Dan 7:9), and we do not say that he was in ancient days, but he was ancient of days; for he was before days, before all time; and it is equal to the ancient of days to be existing before the ages, as it has been said: 'the one existing before the ages' (Rev 1:8). 'Your hand' therefore 'destroyed nations'. Your punishing power. Those who serve with punishments, angels, are able to be called hands of God, just as we say the hand of a king, and we do not mean the limb of the body of a hand.

And Job, concerning the punishing power—and he himself was the devil—was saying: 'withdraw your hand' (Job 2:3). This therefore he says: 'your hand', that is, the punishing power, or the active power of the persecutors, or your ministering power, 'destroyed nations'. And take the destruction of the nations by way of ascent as the death of men, by doing and the expulsion of life, according to which the nations were strangers to God. 'And you hid' our fathers. And the nations are destroyed because of the evil which they have; for their evil was a land and a city. And those are being hidden by no other than his right hand. But it is not the same...

One hand and the right hand: for the right is always a hand, but not every hand is right; for we have things to say that are performed by the right hand in a praiseworthy manner. Thus it is said in the Psalms: 'You held the right hand of me' (Ps 118:17). The right is the practical power of the good, but the left is the opposing one. And since things done happen from disposition and from thought, which is called 'heart,' it is said that the wise man has his heart to the right, but the fool to the left; here we do not take the places of bodies. But the wise man has a mind thinking rightly, having understanding concerning the intelligible things. But the heart of the fool is to the left, turning only toward the material.

Often the left is found in the writings not regarding pride, but regarding humiliation, as it says in the Song of Songs: 'His renown is upon my head, and his right shall embrace me' (Song 7:1). And concerning her wisdom it is said: 'For length of days and years of life are in the right' (Prov 3:16)—and the length is the immortal, the things not being destroyed—'but in her left, wealth and glory.' And it gives wealth that is sensible. And these gifts of the hand of wisdom on the left are not trivial.

3–4 You harmed the people and drove them out; for they did not inherit the land by their sword, and their arm did not save them. Those whom you drove out, you drove out having harmed them. But you brought harm upon them so that they might be disciplined. Often harm disciplines; for we do not speak here of harm from sin, but of harm from corrective discipline. Since, therefore, they did not attend to the corrective discipline as is necessary, they were moreover driven out and rejected. 'For they did not inherit the land by their sword' (Ps 106:11). Our fathers, having taken the history of those driven from the land, did not possess the land taken from them by their own war, nor by their own power; 'for not by their sword, nor their arm' prevailed over them, 'but your right and your arm and the light of your face' (Ps 106:11). There is the light, and the salvation.

Through which, therefore, the harm and the driving out happen, is simply a hand. Thus also in one of the Psalms concerning Christ it is said: 'And he shall put his hand in the sea and his right in the rivers' (Ps 74:3). There where there is salt and brine, the hand is simply placed against the evil powers; evil...

title: The Horn as Strength and Divine Name
english: For the powers are now revealed through the sea. 'He said' 'rivers on the right.' For the prophets are rivers, streams flowing from the source of the water that is 'leaping into eternal life' (John 7:38). For 'he who believes' 'in me, as the scripture said, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly' (John 7:38). This indeed he was speaking concerning the Spirit whom the believers were about to receive.

These, being rivers, 'shall strike with the hand upon itself.' And it is a practice of harmony. See then, the hand, where the sea is, the saltiness, the dizziness. But your right hand and your arm and the light of your face. The right hand possesses and an arm suitable. You did not inherit the land by your own hand or by your own arm, but the arm of God and the right hand and the light of his own face provided this to you.

In one way, this is for tropology: that you were not liberated and became in the holy land by your own power or by your own deed. But if you take it with a higher allegory, both his arm and his right hand and the light of his own face are the Savior. Therefore, not in themselves, but in this you were saved, you were migrated from the land of bondage into the good one.

Having prepared, he triumphed, but with God having fought alongside, as the [scripture says]: 'not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of the God who shows mercy' (Romans 9:16). For you were pleased in them. You are yourself my king and my God (Psalm 146:5). For you are not only my God being my Creator and leading me toward my being, but also king, because by providence I rule, no longer being entangled in 'the affairs of life.' And indeed you are my God, I am a creation of God—and every creation has God as God—but as you rule.

He who commands the salvations of Jacob (Hebrews 1:5). To Jacob, who is fleeing from evil, the king and being God commands the salvations. And salvations are commanded to the spirits who minister the salvations, concerning which the apostle says: 'Are not all [of them] ministering spirits sent for the service of those who are about to inherit salvation?' (Hebrews 1:14). Not so that they might confirm and give it, but so that, having heard it, they might proclaim it beforehand.

"Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Behold, your savior is coming'" (Zephaniah 3:17). The 'salvations' of 'Jacob' may be the virtues according to kind, or the two virtues: the practical and the contemplative—the contemplation of truth and the productive [virtue] of praiseworthy works.

"We strike with horns our enemies in you" (Psalm 68:1). You see, we do not strike our enemies using physical horns; you are our horn and our defense. Therefore, you have that which is said in one of the Psalms by all the saints: "And in your favor our horn shall be exalted" (Psalm 92:10). It is not the physical [horn]; for the horn of those possessing it is again a defense. Through it, they will repel the approaching evils. Thus, those who have you as king and God do not have any other horn besides you. For instance, the word attributes something in one of the Twelve: "Those who say, 'We do not have horns in our strength'" (Psalm 75:10). Having a horn and having power, we strike our enemies with horns. Because of this, the horns of these are also crushed: "and all the horns of the sinner I will break" (Psalm 75:10). It is also possible for a king and a kingdom to receive a horn, as it is presented in Daniel: "the ten horns, ten kingdoms" (Daniel 7:24). Therefore, having you as king, we have you as a horn, and "we strike our enemies in you." And "in your name," since we have your designation upon ourselves, "we render powerless" all "those who rise up against us," having an invincible weapon: your designation. However, one must possess a designation, and not merely a hollow one. Not everyone who calls himself a Christian truly possesses the name of Christ, but rather he who is a Christian. "And in your name we rendered powerless those who rise up against us." And from this it is shown again that they rise up against us by premeditated will. They are not such by nature, nor are the [unjust/wicked] such by nature, as those who argue from natures say.

"For I do not hope in my bow, and my sword will not save me" (Psalm 118:95). I indeed have a bow and a sword, since I am clothed in "the full armor of God," but I do not hope in these; not the whole of my expectation is in these, using them. I wish to have God as an ally and a champion, so that I may have the strength to strike against those to whom I send my...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Confession and Divine Deliverance
english: arrows, and that my sword [be] timely... opposing ones. But these are invisible. Often the sword of those possessing the word is said: 'who have sharpened their tongues like a sword' (Ps 57:9); and 'sons of men, their teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp knife' (Ps 63:7). And another [saying]: 'his sword upon his thigh' (1 Sam 2:26). They possess swords not only 'in their hands', but also upon their thighs. And perhaps the discourses concerning temperance, which kill 'the members upon the earth' (Col 3:5), are swords upon the thigh.

Often also the things of generation are signified through the name of the thigh. For when it says in Ezekiel: 'and every thigh shall be moistened with moisture' (Ezek 47:9), this means: all are unrestrained, pursuing the moisture of pleasures. For you saved us from those who afflict us. Since you saved us also from those who afflict us, we knew that 'in you we gore our enemies' (Ps 118:145). Because of this, then, since this has surpassed us from you, we knew that one must not hope in the bow—to use it, indeed, but not as having shot through it irretrievably. And [you turn] those who hate us to shame.

Those who hate have a difference again from those who afflict, sometimes by the underlying substance and sometimes by the thought. Often the same ones both afflict and hate, and these are the same according to the underlying substance. Sometimes, however, the one hating is not able to be an enemy when he is weak; for the weak one is able to hate, but he is not able to act as an enemy from the manifest [action], for it would harm him. Moreover, even if they differ only in thought according to the underlying substance, even if they are different ones and others, God delivers and saves from these and puts them to shame.

'In God we shall be praised all the day long' (Ps 52:7). Of those being praised, some are praised for the beauty of the body, others because of strength. The stout ones are praised in strength, others in another skill, and others because of wealth, because of nobility; but in you we shall be praised. We have no cause for praise other than you; for even if we have hardship, since through you we have attained these things and 'in God we do power' (Rom 16:25), in you we have the praise. Often the day signifies the time of the life of those saying, as: 'for your sake we are dying all...' (Rom 7:24).

...the whole day, that is, through life. And we shall confess in your name forever. This calling of yours provides much power to us. For in it indeed we 'despise' all 'those who rise up against us'. Therefore 'in your name we shall confess forever'. The name of the confession here signifies thanksgiving: 'I will confess to you, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and have revealed them to infants' (Matt 11:25). In order that it may be a gift, it is possible to say thus: 'in your name we shall confess', because it has become to us a cause of salvation. And it is also possible to say this: in your name which has been invoked upon us, as if you are saying: in knowledge or in virtue I shall confess.

Psalm. But now you have saved and protected us, and you will not let go in the powers of our own. 'You are the same, my king and my God' (Ps 145:11). [Allusion to Ps 145/146] The voice to God; for those approaching and drawing near... God is king. 'He who commands the salvations of Jacob' (Ps 146:7). To those near... he commands the salvations and all good things. Concerning this he says: 'In you we shall be praised all the day and in your name we shall confess forever' (Ps 118:35), that is, we shall give thanks. And he says: 'But now you have saved and protected us, and you will not let go in the powers of our own'. When he went out in the powers of our own, his military power or by the power of our strength, we always prevailed. And everything contrary exists here for us.

And since I was saying—it is not necessary to speak the problematic things explicitly about them—Israel, sinning, was driven from Jerusalem to Babylon in the manner of captivity. And Daniel and those three and Joshua the son of Nun and Ezekiel and the others of the Twelve Prophets were there, Haggai and Zechariah. These were not taken into Babylon in the manner of captivity, but for the sake of being a participant, helping and healing those condemned there. God condemns someone with mercy, that is, he does not leave him without help. And he sends angels and makes holy men to fall and be harmed and in captivity, not because of their own sins, but for the sake of the salvation of others.
